issues.detail: Edge cases like partial rotation recovery, complex validation rules (format/range), and conditional variable requirements (required only in specific environments) are not addressed.

Environment comparison procedure lacks automation; matrix building requires manual inspection of CI/CD platforms and hosting dashboards, and platform-specific rotation procedures (Stripe, SendGrid, etc.) are too generic.
Bash-specific grep commands and Node.js validation script assume Unix/macOS; Windows PowerShell equivalents and guidance for non-JavaScript projects (Python, Go, Rust) are minimal or absent.

scenarios.name: audit-env-variables
scenarios.rationale: Response A asks for prerequisites instead of auditing; Response B performs the required audit, identifies undocumented variables and crash-prone references with file locations, but lacks explicit grep commands and comprehensive comparison table between code usage and .env.example.

scenarios.name: compare-staging-production
scenarios.rationale: Both responses fail to deliver the required audit (no comparison matrix, no missing-variable flags, no identical-secret detection, no variable-type classification), but B is more actionable by proposing specific grep commands to discover what env vars the code references, whereas A only asks what information is available and defers the entire audit to the user providing data first.

scenarios.name: rotate-jwt-secret-safe
scenarios.rationale: Response A omits grep commands entirely and doesn't explicitly verify for hardcoded secrets—critical rubric requirements—despite providing excellent phase-based logic and detailed NestJS code. Response B includes specific grep commands for locating all JWT_SECRET usages and helper functions, meets all four rubric criteria, though could be more explicit about hardcoded-value detection.
